svg.title: Apply this first to JR, then to composition with the fine response T, then to multiplication by J′T. The bound for T retains its factor L−2 throughout, so the mixed row costs CfL−2. The normal row s−1d′TJ′T has an L-independent bound, as do I −J′R′J′T and PeR′J′T. Stacking takes their maximum. Choose one upper price covering these and the original input prices. Keep A0, T unchanged; every carried fine difference keeps its L−1−r or L−2−r bound at the reduced width and enlarged price. This proves the estimates named F08; positivity and the Gram identity are separate algebraic statements proved here. On a fixed pair of tori put W = JTJ and W ′ = J′TJ′, the fine and coarse metrics from the full Gram rows. Let R = W −1 and R′ = W ′−1.
